question:
Which of the following options is NOT correct about plant cells?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Cell wall of a plant cell is made up of cellulose.
The plant cells cannot divide by mitosis.
A plant cell usually contains a large vacuole.
Generally, all plant cells contain chloroplast.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The plant cells cannot divide by mitosis.

Explanation:
Plant cells can divide by mitosis. Mitosis is a type of cell division where a mother cell divides into two identical daughter cells. This process is essential for growth and repair in plants. The other options are correct: the cell wall of a plant cell is made of cellulose, which provides mechanical support. Plant cells usually contain a large vacuole that helps maintain cell shape. However, not all plant cells contain chloroplasts; they are found only in green parts (like leaves) and are absent in parts like roots.

Extra Facts:
Plant cells contain certain organelles not found in animal cells, such as chloroplasts, which are responsible for photosynthesis. Plant cells also contain plastids, which can be of different types, such as leucoplasts (starch storage) and chromoplasts (pigments). The cell wall provides structural support and is composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin. Vacuoles in plant cells are filled with cell sap, which helps maintain turgor pressure.

☛ In which organelle does photosynthesis occur? → Chloroplast
☛ What is the function of vacuoles in plant cells? → Maintain cell shape
☛ Which organelle is absent in animal cells? → Cell wall
☛ What is mitochondria called? → Powerhouse of the cell

आमतौर पर, सभी पादप कोशिकाओं में हरितलवक (क्लोरोप्लास्ट) होता है।
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है पादप कोशिकाएँ समसूत्री विभाजन द्वारा विभाजित नहीं हो सकतीं।

Explanation:
पादप कोशिकाएँ समसूत्री विभाजन (माइटोसिस) द्वारा विभाजित हो सकती हैं। माइटोसिस एक प्रकार का कोशिका विभाजन है जिसमें एक मातृ कोशिका दो समान संतति कोशिकाओं में विभाजित होती है। यह प्रक्रिया पादपों में वृद्धि और मरम्मत के लिए आवश्यक है। अन्य विकल्प सही हैं: पादप कोशिका की कोशिका भित्ति सेल्यूलोज से बनी होती है, जो उन्हें यांत्रिक सहायता प्रदान करती है। पादप कोशिकाओं में आमतौर पर एक बड़ी रिक्तिका होती है जो कोशिका के आकार को बनाए रखने में मदद करती है। हालांकि, सभी पादप कोशिकाओं में हरितलवक (क्लोरोप्लास्ट) नहीं होता; यह केवल हरे भागों (जैसे पत्तियों) में पाया जाता है, जबकि जड़ों जैसे भागों में अनुपस्थित होता है।

Extra Facts:
पादप कोशिकाओं में कुछ विशेष अंगक होते हैं जो जंतु कोशिकाओं में नहीं पाए जाते, जैसे हरितलवक (क्लोरोप्लास्ट), जो प्रकाश संश्लेषण के लिए जिम्मेदार होते हैं। पादप कोशिकाओं में प्लास्टिड भी होते हैं, जो विभिन्न प्रकार के हो सकते हैं, जैसे कि ल्यूकोप्लास्ट (स्टार्च संग्रह) और क्रोमोप्लास्ट (रंगद्रव्य)। कोशिका भित्ति पादप कोशिकाओं को संरचनात्मक सहायता प्रदान करती है और यह सेल्यूलोज, हेमिकेल्यूलोज और पेक्टिन से बनी होती है। पादप कोशिकाओं में रिक्तिकाएँ कोशिका रस से भरी होती हैं, जो कोशिका के टर्गर दबाव को बनाए रखने में मदद करती हैं।

question:
In which year did Robert Brown observe the zigzag movement of colloidal particles in solution?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: 1829
1827
1828
1826
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1827

Explanation:
Robert Brown observed the zigzag movement of colloidal particles in a solution in 1827. This motion is known as 'Brownian Motion'. It occurs due to the collision of colloidal particles with solvent molecules. Later, in 1905, Albert Einstein provided a mathematical analysis of this phenomenon, which confirmed the existence of atoms and molecules. This observation became a crucial piece of evidence for the Kinetic Theory.

Extra Facts:
The study of Brownian motion is significant in Physical Chemistry and Nanoscience. It demonstrates that small particles suspended in a fluid (liquid or gas) exhibit continuous random motion. This discovery strengthened the Atomic Theory. Brownian motion is also applied in Colloidal Science, Biophysics, and Meteorology.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ Who discovered Brownian Motion? → Robert Brown
☛ Brownian Motion is evidence of which theory? → Kinetic Theory
☛ When did Einstein analyze Brownian Motion? → 1905
☛ What causes the motion of colloidal particles? → Collision with solvent molecules

question:
Around which year did Robert Brown publish a paper highlighting the presence of a nucleus in plant cells ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1780s
1950s
1830s
1660s
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1830s

Explanation:
Robert Brown published a paper around 1831-1833 highlighting the presence of the nucleus in plant cells. This discovery was a significant milestone in Cell Biology. Brown identified the nucleus while studying the cells of orchid plants. The nucleus is a vital organelle that stores genetic material (DNA) and controls cellular functions. This discovery contributed significantly to the development of the Cell Theory, which was later proposed by Schleiden and Schwann in 1839. The nucleus is now known to be the control center of the cell, containing chromosomes that carry hereditary information.

Extra Facts:
1. Robert Brown was a Scottish botanist who also discovered Brownian Motion, which describes the random movement of particles in a fluid.
2. According to the Cell Theory, all living organisms are composed of cells, and the cell is the basic unit of life.
3. The nucleus contains chromosomes, which are made of DNA molecules and carry genetic information essential for inheritance and cellular functions.

☛ What is the difference between plant and animal cells? → Plant cells have a cell wall
☛ What is the full form of DNA? → Deoxyribonucleic Acid
☛ What type of cell division is mitosis? → Equational division

question:
The cells having well-organized nucleus with a nuclear membrane are designated as__________ .

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Cheek cells
prokaryotic cells
eukaryotic cells
autokaryotic cells
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is eukaryotic cells

Explanation:
Eukaryotic cells are characterized by a well-defined nucleus enclosed within a nuclear membrane. These cells contain membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, and endoplasmic reticulum, which perform specialized functions. Eukaryotic cells have a complex structure, and their genetic material (DNA) is organized within the nucleus. They are found in multicellular organisms (e.g., humans, plants, animals) and some unicellular organisms (e.g., amoeba, yeast).

Extra Facts:
Prokaryotic cells lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, and their DNA floats freely in the cytoplasm. Examples include bacteria and archaea. Eukaryotic cells divide through mitosis and meiosis, while prokaryotes reproduce via binary fission. Eukaryotic cells are generally larger and more complex than prokaryotic cells.

☛ Which type of cells contain mitochondria? → Eukaryotic cells
☛ What type of cell is a bacterium? → Prokaryotic
☛ Where is DNA located in eukaryotic cells? → Nucleus
☛ Which organelle is absent in plant cells? → Centrioles

Explanation:
यूकेरियोटिक कोशिकाएं वे कोशिकाएं हैं जिनमें एक सुव्यवस्थित केंद्रक होता है जो एक परमाणु झिल्ली (nuclear membrane) से घिरा होता है। इन कोशिकाओं में अन्य कोशिकांग (organelles) भी होते हैं जैसे माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया, गॉल्जी उपकरण, और एंडोप्लाज्मिक रेटिकुलम, जो विभिन्न जैविक कार्यों को संपादित करते हैं। ये कोशिकाएं जटिल संरचना वाली होती हैं और इनमें आनुवंशिक सामग्री (DNA) केंद्रक के अंदर संगठित रूप में होती है। यूकेरियोटिक कोशिकाएं बहुकोशिकीय जीवों (जैसे मनुष्य, पौधे, जानवर) और कुछ एककोशिकीय जीवों (जैसे अमीबा, यीस्ट) में पाई जाती हैं।

Extra Facts:
प्रोकैरियोटिक कोशिकाएं यूकेरियोटिक कोशिकाओं से भिन्न होती हैं क्योंकि इनमें केंद्रक नहीं होता और इनका DNA कोशिकाद्रव्य में स्वतंत्र रूप से बिखरा होता है। बैक्टीरिया और आर्किया प्रोकैरियोटिक कोशिकाओं के उदाहरण हैं। यूकेरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में कोशिका विभाजन माइटोसिस और मियोसिस द्वारा होता है, जबकि प्रोकैरियोट्स में बाइनरी फिशन (द्विखंडन) होता है।

question:
The bodies of living organisms are made of tiny units called __________.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: genes
centrioles
buds
cells
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is cells

Explanation:
The bodies of living organisms are made of tiny units called 'cells'. Cells are the basic structural and functional units of life. All living organisms are composed of one or more cells. According to the cell theory, all living things are made up of cells, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells. Cells carry out various biological processes such as respiration, nutrition, excretion, and reproduction. They also contain genetic material (DNA), which controls the growth and functions of organisms.

Extra Facts:
1. The cell was discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665 when he observed a thin slice of cork under a microscope.
2. Cells are of two types: prokaryotic (e.g., bacteria) and eukaryotic (e.g., plants and animals).
3. The human body consists of approximately 37 trillion cells, which vary in type, such as nerve cells, muscle cells, and blood cells.

☛ Which organelle is found in plant cells but not in animal cells? → Chloroplast

☛ Who proposed the cell theory? → Schleiden and Schwann

question:
Which of the following is NOT a function of mesosomes?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content
Locomotion
Respiration
DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Locomotion

Explanation:
Mesosomes are invaginations of the plasma membrane in prokaryotic cells (e.g., bacteria). Their primary functions include:
1. Increasing the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content: This is crucial for respiration and other metabolic activities.
2. Respiration: Mesosomes contain respiratory enzymes that aid in ATP production.
3. DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells: Mesosomes help segregate DNA during cell division.
Locomotion is NOT a function of mesosomes. In bacteria, locomotion is facilitated by flagella or other structures, not mesosomes.

Extra Facts:
1. Mesosomes were discovered in the 1950s, but modern research questions their existence, suggesting they may be artifacts of sample preparation.
2. Mesosomes contain respiratory chain enzymes (e.g., cytochromes) involved in oxidative phosphorylation.
3. Prokaryotic cells lack mitochondria, so respiratory functions are performed by the plasma membrane and mesosomes.

question:
The nucleus is separated from _______ by a nuclear membrane.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: cytoplasm
cell
gene
vacuole
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is cytoplasm

Explanation:
The nucleus is separated from the cytoplasm by a double-layered membrane called the nuclear membrane (or nuclear envelope). This membrane protects the genetic material (DNA) inside the nucleus and regulates the exchange of materials between the nucleus and cytoplasm through small openings called nuclear pores. The nuclear membrane is made up of lipids and proteins and disintegrates during cell division, reforming afterward.

Extra Facts:
• The nuclear membrane is absent in prokaryotic cells (e.g., bacteria), where DNA floats freely in the cytoplasm.
• Nuclear pores allow selective transport of RNA and proteins.
• The nuclear membrane is part of the endomembrane system, which includes the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus.
• Disruption of the nuclear membrane is a key feature of mitosis and meiosis.

question:
A tunnel that runs through the cell wall between two plant cells is known as:

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: ribosome
protoplasm
peroxisome
plasmodesmata
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is plasmodesmata

Explanation:
The microscopic channels that pass through the cell walls of plant cells and connect the cytoplasm of adjacent cells are called plasmodesmata. These structures facilitate the transport and communication between plant cells by allowing the movement of ions, small molecules, and even larger molecules like proteins. Plasmodesmata play a crucial role in cell-to-cell signaling and coordination in plants, ensuring proper growth and response to environmental stimuli.

Extra Facts:
Plasmodesmata are unique to plant cells, as animal cells use gap junctions for intercellular communication. The presence of a rigid cell wall in plant cells necessitates plasmodesmata for maintaining cytoplasmic continuity. These structures form during cytokinesis and vary in number and size depending on the plant tissue. Plasmodesmata are dynamic and can regulate their permeability in response to developmental or environmental cues.

question:
In which year did E Gorter and F Grendel make a breakthrough by examining the surface area of lipids and concluded that the lipid surface surrounding cells must be of two layers?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1910
1925
1945
1962
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1925

Explanation:
E. Gorter and F. Grendel made a significant breakthrough in 1925 by examining the surface area of lipids. They extracted lipids from red blood cells (RBCs) and studied their surface area. They found that the lipid area was twice the surface area of the cell membrane. From this, they concluded that the cell membrane must have a bilayer (double-layer) structure. This discovery was a milestone in understanding the structure of the cell membrane and laid the foundation for modern cell biology.

Extra Facts:
☛ The bilayer structure of the cell membrane consists of phospholipids, with hydrophilic (water-attracting) heads facing outward and hydrophobic (water-repelling) tails facing inward.
☛ This model is called the lipid bilayer model and explains the semi-permeability of the cell membrane.
☛ Later, in 1972, Singer and Nicolson proposed the Fluid Mosaic Model, which better explains the structure and function of the cell membrane.

question:
Which type of haploid unicellular eukaryote cells has a diameter of ~10 μm, and about half of their volume is occupied by cup-shaped chloroplasts ?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Hydrodictyon
Ulva
Chlamydomonas
Oedogonium
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chlamydomonas

Explanation:
Chlamydomonas is a haploid unicellular eukaryotic alga with a diameter of approximately 10 μm. About half of its cell volume is occupied by a cup-shaped chloroplast, which is involved in photosynthesis. Chlamydomonas contains a large cup-shaped chloroplast with a pyrenoid, which plays a crucial role in starch synthesis. This alga is found in freshwater and possesses two flagella that aid in locomotion.

Extra Facts:
Chlamydomonas is classified as a 'green alga' and belongs to the Chlorophyta group. It can reproduce both asexually (via zoospores) and sexually (via gametes). Chlamydomonas is an important model organism in genetics and cell biology due to its simple eukaryotic structure. It is widely studied for understanding photosynthesis, flagellar movement, and cellular responses to light (phototaxis).

☛ What type of alga is Chlamydomonas? → Green alga

☛ Where is Chlamydomonas found? → Freshwater
☛ What is the shape of the chloroplast in Chlamydomonas? → Cup-shaped
question_hi:

अल्वा
क्लैमाइडोमोनस
ऊडोगोनियम
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है क्लैमाइडोमोनस

Explanation:
क्लैमाइडोमोनस एक अगुणित (haploid) एककोशिकीय यूकेरियोटिक शैवाल है जिसका व्यास लगभग 10 μm होता है। इसकी कोशिका का लगभग आधा आयतन कप के आकार के क्लोरोप्लास्ट द्वारा घिरा होता है, जिसमें प्रकाश संश्लेषण (photosynthesis) होता है। क्लैमाइडोमोनस में एक बड़ा कप के आकार का क्लोरोप्लास्ट होता है जिसमें पाइरेनॉइड (pyrenoid) पाया जाता है, जो स्टार्च संश्लेषण में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। यह शैवाल मीठे पानी में पाया जाता है और इसकी कोशिका में दो फ्लैगेला (flagella) होते हैं जो गति में सहायता करते हैं।

Extra Facts:

question:
The outermost cover of plant cells is/are known as______.

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Cell membrane
Lysosomes
Cell wall
Golgi apparatus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cell Wall

Explanation:
The outermost covering of plant cells is called the Cell Wall. It is a rigid, tough, and permeable structure primarily composed of cellulose. The cell wall provides structural support, gives shape to the cell, and offers mechanical protection. It is located outside the cell membrane and is absent in animal cells. The cell wall prevents plant cells from bursting due to external pressures like osmotic water absorption.

Extra Facts:
- The cell wall contains polysaccharides such as cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin.
- It is divided into the primary cell wall and the secondary cell wall.
- Some plant cells contain lignin, which makes wood rigid.
- Bacteria and fungi also have cell walls, but their composition differs from that of plants.

☛ Do animal cells have a cell wall? → No
☛ What is the cell wall mainly made of? → Cellulose
☛ What is called the 'powerhouse' of a plant cell? → Mitochondria
☛ Where does photosynthesis occur? → Chloroplast
question_hi:
पादप कोशिकाओं का सबसे बाहरी आवरण क्या कहलाता है?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options_hi: कोशिका झिल्ली (Cell Membrane)
लाइसोसोम (Lysosomes)
कोशिका भित्ति (Cell Wall)
गॉल्जीकाय (Golgi Apparatus)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कोशिका भित्ति (Cell Wall)

Explanation:
पादप कोशिकाओं का सबसे बाहरी आवरण कोशिका भित्ति (Cell Wall) होता है। यह एक कठोर, सख्त और पारगम्य संरचना है जो मुख्य रूप से सेल्यूलोज (Cellulose) से बनी होती है। कोशिका भित्ति पादप कोशिकाओं को संरचनात्मक सहायता प्रदान करती है, उन्हें आकार देती है और यांत्रिक सुरक्षा प्रदान करती है। यह कोशिका झिल्ली (Cell Membrane) के बाहर स्थित होती है और जंतु कोशिकाओं में अनुपस्थित होती है। कोशिका भित्ति पादपों को बाह्य दबावों, जैसे पानी का अंतःशोषण (Osmosis), से बचाती है और कोशिका के विस्फोट (Lysis) को रोकती है।

Extra Facts:
- कोशिका भित्ति में सेल्यूलोज, हेमिकेल्यूलोज और पेक्टिन जैसे पॉलीसेकेराइड्स पाए जाते हैं।
- यह प्राथमिक कोशिका भित्ति (Primary Cell Wall) और द्वितीयक कोशिका भित्ति (Secondary Cell Wall) में विभाजित होती है।
- कुछ पादप कोशिकाओं में लिग्निन (Lignin) भी पाया जाता है, जो लकड़ी को कठोर बनाता है।
- जीवाणुओं (Bacteria) और कवक (Fungi) में भी कोशिका भित्ति होती है, लेकिन उनकी संरचना पादपों से भिन्न होती है।

question:
Plant cell has a big central_______ unlike a number of small_________ in animal cells.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Vacuole, vacuoles
Cell wall, cell walls
Tissue, tissues
Cell membrane, cell membranes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vacuole, vacuoles

Explanation:
Plant cells contain a large central vacuole that occupies most of the cell's volume and stores cell sap. It provides structural support and helps in the storage of nutrients, waste products, and water. In contrast, animal cells have multiple small vacuoles that assist in functions like food storage, waste disposal, and water regulation.

Extra Facts:
Vacuoles are membrane-bound structures called tonoplasts. In plant cells, the vacuole maintains turgor pressure, which keeps the plant upright. Animal cell vacuoles are less prominent and mainly involved in endocytosis and exocytosis processes.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is the main difference between plant and animal cells? → Plant cells have a cell wall and a large vacuole, while animal cells do not.
☛ What is the primary function of the vacuole in plant cells? → Structural support and storage of substances.
☛ How are vacuoles in animal cells structured? → Small and numerous.
☛ What is the membrane surrounding the vacuole in plant cells called? → Tonoplast.
☛ What does the vacuole in plant cells help maintain? → Turgor pressure.

रिक्तिकाएँ कोशिका के अंदर एक झिल्लीदार संरचना होती हैं, जिन्हें टोनोप्लास्ट कहा जाता है। पादप कोशिकाओं में रिक्तिका का आकार कोशिका के दबाव (टर्गर प्रेशर) को बनाए रखने में मदद करता है, जिससे पौधे सीधे खड़े रहते हैं। जंतु कोशिकाओं में रिक्तिकाएँ कम प्रमुख होती हैं और मुख्य रूप से एंडोसाइटोसिस और एक्सोसाइटोसिस प्रक्रियाओं में शामिल होती हैं।

question:
Which cytologist demonstrated the role of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) in protein processing and sorting in a variety of cells in the 1960s ?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Ralph M Steinman
George E Palade
Nettie Stevens
Cyril Darlington
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is George E Palade

Explanation:
George E Palade was a renowned cytologist who, in the 1960s, elucidated the role of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) in protein synthesis, processing, and sorting. Using electron microscopy, he studied cellular structures and discovered that ER, when bound with ribosomes, assists in protein synthesis. His groundbreaking work earned him the Nobel Prize in 1974. The ER exists in two forms: rough ER (ribosome-attached) and smooth ER (involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification).

Extra Facts:
☛ George E Palade also contributed to the understanding of mitochondria and Golgi apparatus.
☛ The ER plays a crucial role in protein folding, calcium ion storage, and lipid production.
☛ Rough ER contains ribosomes for protein synthesis, while smooth ER aids in detoxification and hormone production.

☛ Where does protein synthesis occur? → Ribosomes

☛ What is the role of lysosomes? → Digest cellular waste

question:
Who discovered a cell?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Rudolf Virchow
Theodor Schwann
Matthias Schleiden

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Robert Hooke

Explanation:
Robert Hooke discovered the cell in 1665. He observed a thin slice of cork under a microscope and noticed small, room-like structures, which he named 'cells'. This discovery was published in his book 'Micrographia'. However, he actually saw the cell walls of dead cells. Later, Theodor Schwann and Matthias Schleiden proposed the cell theory, stating that all living organisms are composed of cells. Rudolf Virchow further expanded this theory by stating that all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

Extra Facts:
The cell theory has three main principles: (1) All living organisms are composed of one or more cells, (2) The cell is the basic unit of life, and (3) All cells arise from pre-existing cells. This theory forms the foundation of modern biology. Cells are of two types: prokaryotic (e.g., bacteria) and eukaryotic (e.g., plants and animals). Eukaryotic cells are more complex and contain a nucleus.

question:

II. Muscle cells - Spindle shape

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Only II
Neither I nor II
Only I
Both I and II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both I and II

Explanation:
The shape of cells varies according to their functions. Red blood cells (RBCs) in humans are spherical and biconcave (indented on both sides), which provides them with a larger surface area for the transport of oxygen and carbon dioxide. This shape also helps them pass through narrow capillaries easily. Muscle cells are spindle-shaped, which allows them to contract and expand efficiently. This shape makes muscles flexible and strong, enabling body movements.

Extra Facts:
Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, which binds oxygen. They lack a nucleus, allowing more space for hemoglobin. Muscle cells are of three types: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth. Skeletal muscles are voluntary and striated, while smooth muscles are involuntary and found in internal organs. Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart and is involuntary and striated.

कोशिका द्रव्य में पाए जाने वाले राइबोसोम, माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और गॉल्जी निकाय जैसे संरचनाएँ कोशिकांग कहलाती हैं। कोशिकांग कोशिका के अंदर विशिष्ट कार्य करने वाली संरचनाएँ होती हैं। उदाहरण के लिए, राइबोसोम प्रोटीन संश्लेषण, माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया ऊर्जा उत्पादन (ATP), और गॉल्जी निकाय प्रोटीन संशोधन और पैकेजिंग के लिए जिम्मेदार होते हैं। ये सभी कोशिकांग कोशिका के सुचारू संचालन और जीवन प्रक्रियाओं के लिए आवश्यक हैं।

Extra Facts:
कोशिकांग यूकेरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में पाए जाते हैं, जबकि प्रोकैरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में इनकी अनुपस्थिति होती है। माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया को 'कोशिका का पावरहाउस' कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह ATP (एडेनोसिन ट्राइफॉस्फेट) उत्पन्न करता है। गॉल्जी निकाय की खोज कैमिलो गॉल्जी ने की थी और इसका नाम उन्हीं के नाम पर रखा गया। राइबोसोम RNA और प्रोटीन से बने होते हैं और ये प्रोकैरियोट्स और यूकेरियोट्स दोनों में पाए जाते हैं।

question:
What is the fourth step in mitosis where non-kinetochore spindle fibres lengthen and elongate the cell ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Telophase
Metaphase
Anaphase
Prophase
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Anaphase

Explanation:
The fourth stage of mitosis is Anaphase. In this stage, non-kinetochore spindle fibres elongate and stretch the cell, while kinetochore spindle fibres contract and pull the chromosomes toward opposite poles. This ensures equal distribution of genetic material to the daughter cells. Anaphase is followed by Telophase, where two distinct nuclei form in the dividing cell.

Extra Facts:
☛ Mitosis is a cell division process where a parent cell divides into two genetically identical daughter cells.
☛ The four main stages of mitosis are: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.
☛ Cytokinesis occurs after mitosis, dividing the cytoplasm to form two separate cells.
☛ Mitosis plays a crucial role in growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction.

☛ In which stage do chromosomes move to opposite poles? → Anaphase

☛ In which type of reproduction does mitosis occur? → Asexual Reproduction
question_hi:
सूत्री विभाजन (Mitosis) की चौथी अवस्था क्या है जिसमें गैर-काइनेटोकोर तर्कुतंतु कोशिका को लंबी करती हैं और बढ़ाती हैं?

options_hi: अंत्यावस्था (Telophase)
मध्यावस्था (Metaphase)
पश्चावस्था (Anaphase)
पूर्वावस्था (Prophase)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है पश्चावस्था (Anaphase)

Explanation:
सूत्री विभाजन (Mitosis) की चौथी अवस्था पश्चावस्था (Anaphase) होती है। इस अवस्था में, गैर-काइनेटोकोर तर्कुतंतु (Non-Kinetochore Spindle Fibres) कोशिका को लंबा करने और बढ़ाने का कार्य करते हैं। इसके अलावा, काइनेटोकोर तर्कुतंतु (Kinetochore Spindle Fibres) संकुचित होकर गुणसूत्रों (Chromosomes) को विपरीत ध्रुवों (Poles) की ओर खींचते हैं। यह प्रक्रिया कोशिका विभाजन के दौरान आनुवंशिक सामग्री (Genetic Material) के समान वितरण को सुनिश्चित करती है। पश्चावस्था के बाद अंत्यावस्था (Telophase) आती है, जिसमें कोशिका दो अलग-अलग नाभिक (Nuclei) बनाती है।

Extra Facts:
☛ माइटोसिस (Mitosis) एक कोशिका विभाजन प्रक्रिया है जिसमें एक मातृ कोशिका (Parent Cell) दो समान संतति कोशिकाओं (Daughter Cells) में विभाजित होती है।
☛ माइटोसिस के चार मुख्य चरण हैं: पूर्वावस्था (Prophase), मध्यावस्था (Metaphase), पश्चावस्था (Anaphase), और अंत्यावस्था (Telophase)।
☛ साइटोकाइनेसिस (Cytokinesis) माइटोसिस के बाद होता है, जिसमें कोशिका द्रव्य (Cytoplasm) विभाजित होता है और दो अलग कोशिकाएं बनती हैं।
☛ माइटोसिस शरीर की वृद्धि, मरम्मत और अलैंगिक प्रजनन (Asexual Reproduction) में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है।

question:
The cells having nuclear material without nuclear membrane are termed as____.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Cheek cells
Prokaryotic cells
Eukaryotic cells
Onion cells
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prokaryotic cells

Explanation:
Prokaryotic cells are those cells that lack a nuclear membrane, and their nuclear material (DNA) remains freely scattered in the cytoplasm. These cells also lack membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, Golgi bodies, and endoplasmic reticulum. They are smaller in size and contain only ribosomes as their organelle. Examples of prokaryotic cells include bacteria and cyanobacteria (blue-green algae).

Extra Facts:
☛ Eukaryotic cells have a well-defined nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane and contain various membrane-bound organelles.
☛ Prokaryotic cells possess small circular DNA molecules called plasmids, which are responsible for traits like antibiotic resistance.
☛ Cell division in prokaryotes occurs through binary fission, while eukaryotes divide via mitosis/meiosis.

☛ Where is DNA located in eukaryotic cells? → Nucleus
☛ What type of cell is a bacterium? → Prokaryotic
☛ Which organelle is absent in plant cells? → Centriole
☛ What is mitochondria called? → Powerhouse of the cell

question:
The energy currency of the cell is called as:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: AMP
ATP
DNA
RNA
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is ATP

Explanation:
The energy currency of the cell is called ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate). ATP is a high-energy molecule that stores and transfers energy within cells. It consists of three phosphate groups, and when one phosphate group is broken off, energy is released, forming ADP (Adenosine Diphosphate). This process occurs during cellular respiration, where glucose is oxidized to synthesize ATP. ATP is used in various biological processes such as muscle contraction, protein synthesis, and nerve impulse transmission.

Extra Facts:
ATP is synthesized in the mitochondria, often called the 'powerhouse of the cell'. During photosynthesis, plants also produce ATP. Besides ATP, GTP (Guanosine Triphosphate) provides energy for some cellular processes. ATP was discovered in 1929 by Karl Lohmann. It is the fastest and most convenient energy source for cells.

☛ What is the full form of ATP? → Adenosine Triphosphate

☛ What is the primary energy source in the human body? → Glucose
☛ How many phosphate groups does ADP have? → Two

Explanation:
कोशिका की ऊर्जा मुद्रा ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) कहलाती है। ATP एक उच्च-ऊर्जा यौगिक है जो कोशिकाओं में ऊर्जा का संचय और स्थानांतरण करता है। यह तीन फॉस्फेट समूहों से बना होता है, जिनमें से एक के टूटने पर ऊर्जा मुक्त होती है और ADP (Adenosine Diphosphate) बनता है। यह प्रक्रिया कोशिकीय श्वसन के दौरान होती है, जहां ग्लूकोज का ऑक्सीकरण होता है और ATP संश्लेषित होता है। ATP का उपयोग विभिन्न जैविक प्रक्रियाओं जैसे मांसपेशी संकुचन, प्रोटीन संश्लेषण और तंत्रिका आवेगों के संचरण में किया जाता है।

Extra Facts:
ATP का संश्लेषण माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया में होता है, जिसे कोशिका का 'पावरहाउस' कहा जाता है। प्रकाश संश्लेषण के दौरान पौधों में भी ATP बनता है। ATP के अलावा, GTP (Guanosine Triphosphate) भी कुछ कोशिकीय प्रक्रियाओं में ऊर्जा प्रदान करता है। ATP की खोज 1929 में कार्ल लोहमैन ने की थी। यह कोशिका के लिए ऊर्जा का सबसे तेज और सुविधाजनक स्रोत है।

question:
The cell wall of bacteria is made up of:

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: peptidoglycan
glycogen
cellulose
peptone
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is peptidoglycan

Explanation:
The cell wall of bacteria is primarily composed of peptidoglycan. Peptidoglycan is a complex molecule made up of N-acetylmuramic acid (NAM) and N-acetylglucosamine (NAG), linked together by peptide chains. This cell wall provides structural support to bacteria and protects them from external pressures. The thickness of peptidoglycan varies between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan layer, while Gram-negative bacteria have a thin layer surrounded by an outer membrane.

Extra Facts:
Peptidoglycan is a unique feature of bacteria and distinguishes them from eukaryotic cells. Antibiotics like penicillin kill bacteria by inhibiting peptidoglycan synthesis. Plant cell walls are made of cellulose, while fungal cell walls are composed of chitin. The study of bacterial cell walls is crucial for their classification and determining antibiotic sensitivity.

☛ What is the cell wall of Gram-positive bacteria like? → Thick peptidoglycan layer
☛ What is the plant cell wall made of? → Cellulose
☛ What is the fungal cell wall made of? → Chitin
☛ What does penicillin act on? → Peptidoglycan synthesis
☛ What is the cell wall of Gram-negative bacteria like? → Thin peptidoglycan layer

जीवाणुओं की कोशिका भित्ति मुख्य रूप से पेप्टिडोग्लाइकन से बनी होती है। पेप्टिडोग्लाइकन एक जटिल अणु है जो N-एसिटाइलम्यूरामिक एसिड (NAM) और N-एसिटाइलग्लूकोसामाइन (NAG) से बना होता है, जो पेप्टाइड श्रृंखलाओं से जुड़े होते हैं। यह कोशिका भित्ति जीवाणुओं को संरचनात्मक सहायता प्रदान करती है और उन्हें बाह्य दबावों से बचाती है। ग्राम-पॉजिटिव और ग्राम-नेगेटिव जीवाणुओं में पेप्टिडोग्लाइकन की मोटाई अलग-अलग होती है। ग्राम-पॉजिटिव जीवाणुओं में यह मोटी परत के रूप में होती है, जबकि ग्राम-नेगेटिव जीवाणुओं में यह पतली होती है और एक बाहरी झिल्ली से घिरी होती है।

Extra Facts:
पेप्टिडोग्लाइकन जीवाणुओं की एक विशिष्ट विशेषता है और यह उन्हें यूकेरियोटिक कोशिकाओं से अलग करती है। पेनिसिलिन जैसे एंटीबायोटिक्स पेप्टिडोग्लाइकन संश्लेषण को रोककर जीवाणुओं को मारते हैं। पादप कोशिकाओं की कोशिका भित्ति सेल्यूलोज से बनी होती है, जबकि कवक की कोशिका भित्ति काइटिन से बनी होती है। जीवाणुओं की कोशिका भित्ति का अध्ययन उनके वर्गीकरण और एंटीबायोटिक संवेदनशीलता निर्धारित करने में महत्वपूर्ण है।

question:
Which of the following statement is NOT correct regarding the prokaryotic cell?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: They have only very small ribosomes as organelles
Membrane bound cell organelles are present
Their chromosomes are composed of only nucleic acid.
Their size is generally in the range of 1 - 10 μm
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Membrane bound cell organelles are present

Explanation:
Prokaryotic cells are simple structured cells that lack membrane-bound organelles. They contain only 70S type ribosomes which perform protein synthesis. Their size ranges from 1-10 μm. Prokaryotic cells have a nucleoid which is composed of only DNA, without histone proteins. These cells differ from eukaryotic cells which contain membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria, Golgi bodies etc. The absence of membrane-bound organelles is a defining characteristic of prokaryotes, making the given statement incorrect.

Extra Facts:
Prokaryotic cells are found in bacteria and archaea organisms. They possess a cell wall made of peptidoglycan. They also contain extra-chromosomal DNA called plasmids which are responsible for traits like antibiotic resistance. Prokaryotic cells reproduce asexually through binary fission. These cells are considered one of the earliest life forms to appear on Earth. Prokaryotes play crucial roles in nitrogen fixation, decomposition and many biochemical cycles.

question:
Which among the following is the structural and fundamental unit of life?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Tissue
Enzyme
Cell
Hormone
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cell

Explanation:
The cell is the structural and fundamental unit of life. It is the basic building block of all living organisms. According to the cell theory, all living organisms are composed of cells, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells. The cell contains genetic material (DNA), which controls protein synthesis and other biological processes. A cell can independently perform all life functions, such as respiration, nutrition, excretion, and reproduction. In unicellular organisms, it carries out the entire life cycle, while in multicellular organisms, different types of cells are specialized for specific functions.

Extra Facts:
The cell theory was proposed by Schleiden and Schwann in 1839. Cells are of two types: prokaryotic (e.g., bacteria) and eukaryotic (e.g., plants and animals). Eukaryotic cells have a well-defined nucleus, whereas prokaryotic cells lack a nucleus. The cell membrane (plasma membrane) separates the cell from the external environment and regulates the exchange of materials. Mitochondria are called the 'powerhouse of the cell' because they generate ATP (energy).

☛ What is mitochondria called? → Powerhouse of the cell
☛ What is absent in a prokaryotic cell? → Nucleus
☛ What is lysosome called? → Suicidal bag
question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से क्या जीवन की संरचनात्मक और मौलिक इकाई है?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: ऊतक
किण्वक
कोशिका
हार्मोन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कोशिका

Explanation:
कोशिका जीवन की संरचनात्मक और मौलिक इकाई है। यह सभी जीवों का मूलभूत निर्माण खंड है। कोशिका सिद्धांत के अनुसार, सभी जीव कोशिकाओं से बने होते हैं और सभी कोशिकाएँ पहले से मौजूद कोशिकाओं से ही उत्पन्न होती हैं। कोशिका में आनुवंशिक सामग्री (DNA) होती है, जो प्रोटीन संश्लेषण और अन्य जैविक प्रक्रियाओं को नियंत्रित करती है। कोशिका स्वतंत्र रूप से जीवन के सभी कार्यों को कर सकती है, जैसे कि श्वसन, पोषण, उत्सर्जन और प्रजनन। यह एकल-कोशिकीय जीवों में पूर्ण जीवन चक्र को संचालित करती है और बहु-कोशिकीय जीवों में विशिष्ट कार्यों के लिए विभिन्न प्रकार की कोशिकाएँ विभेदित होती हैं।

Extra Facts:
कोशिका सिद्धांत को 1839 में श्लाइडेन और श्वान ने प्रस्तावित किया था। कोशिकाएँ दो प्रकार की होती हैं: प्रोकैरियोटिक (जैसे बैक्टीरिया) और यूकैरियोटिक (जैसे पौधे और जंतु)। यूकैरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में एक सुव्यवस्थित केन्द्रक होता है, जबकि प्रोकैरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में केन्द्रक नहीं होता। कोशिका झिल्ली (प्लाज्मा मेम्ब्रेन) कोशिका को बाहरी वातावरण से अलग करती है और पदार्थों के आदान-प्रदान को नियंत्रित करती है। माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया कोशिका का 'पावरहाउस' कहलाता है क्योंकि यह ATP (ऊर्जा) उत्पन्न करता है।

question:
Which is the primary structural component responsible for most of the mechanical strength of the cell wall ?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: Heparin
Glycogen
Chitin
Cellulose
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cellulose

Explanation:
Cellulose is the primary structural component responsible for most of the mechanical strength of the cell wall. Cellulose is a polysaccharide composed of long chains of glucose molecules. It is the main structural component of plant cell walls and is often referred to as the 'skeleton of plant cells'. Cellulose molecules are arranged in microfibrils, which provide high tensile strength to the cell wall. This gives plants structural support and helps them withstand external pressures.

Extra Facts:
- Cellulose is the most abundant organic compound on Earth.
- It cannot be digested by humans due to the lack of cellulase enzyme in our digestive system.
- Some bacteria and fungi produce cellulase and can break down cellulose.
- Cellulose is used in the production of paper, textiles, and biofuels.

question_hi:
कोशिका भित्ति की अधिकांश यांत्रिक शक्ति (mechanical strength) के लिए उत्तरदायी प्राथमिक संरचनात्मक घटक कौन-सा है ?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options_hi: हिपैरिन
ग्लाइकोजन
काइटिन
सेलुलोज
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है सेलुलोज

Explanation:
कोशिका भित्ति की अधिकांश यांत्रिक शक्ति के लिए सेलुलोज उत्तरदायी है। सेलुलोज एक पॉलीसेकेराइड है जो ग्लूकोज अणुओं की लंबी श्रृंखला से बना होता है। यह पौधों की कोशिका भित्ति का प्रमुख संरचनात्मक घटक है और इसे 'पादप कोशिका का कंकाल' भी कहा जाता है। सेलुलोज अणु माइक्रोफाइब्रिल्स के रूप में व्यवस्थित होते हैं, जो कोशिका भित्ति को उच्च तन्यता शक्ति (tensile strength) प्रदान करते हैं। यह पौधों को संरचनात्मक सहायता देता है और उन्हें बाहरी दबावों का सामना करने में मदद करता है।

Extra Facts:
- सेलुलोज पृथ्वी पर सबसे प्रचुर मात्रा में पाया जाने वाला कार्बनिक यौगिक है।
- यह मनुष्यों द्वारा पचाया नहीं जा सकता क्योंकि हमारे पास सेल्युलेज एंजाइम (cellulase enzyme) का अभाव होता है।
- कुछ जीवाणु और कवक सेल्युलेज का उत्पादन करते हैं और सेलुलोज को तोड़ सकते हैं।
- सेलुलोज का उपयोग कागज, कपड़ा और जैव ईंधन (biofuel) के उत्पादन में किया जाता है।
